summary: @servicetitan/microfront-tests preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes an opaque bundled payload
details: The package's preinstall lifecycle (setup.mjs) downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync to run a sibling file math_init.js shipped inside the tarball. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (// @bun @bun-cjs header) with obfuscator-style string-array shuffling (WV8StW) whose contents are not human-auditable from source. The advertised library entry (dist/index.js) is an unrelated re-export of ts-mockito test helpers and has no relationship to the payload. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated with hex-suffixed identifiers and per-function string-lookup maps ({ SBBJg: 'bun', dAZFw: 'bun.exe', zjKAu: 'bun-dl-', TdVzu: '/etc/os-release' }) that indirect every constant, further concealing what the install-time code does. Using a freshly downloaded second-language runtime specifically to execute an opaque bundle at install time bypasses tooling that only inspects Node-resolved code, and the cover-story filename math_init does not match the package's stated purpose as a test/mocking helper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
